passages.title: A Disputed Partnership
passages.text: Lichens are often mistaken for a single organism, yet each is a partnership between a fungus and one or more photosynthetic partners, usually green algae or cyanobacteria. The fungus supplies structure, anchoring the lichen to rock or bark and retaining moisture, while the alga manufactures sugars through photosynthesis. For decades after Simon Schwendener proposed this dual hypothesis in 1867, many botanists resisted it, partly because it seemed to dissolve the neat boundaries of taxonomy. The relationship is commonly called mutualism, but some researchers argue that the label flatters the fungus: in laboratory culture the alga can often live perfectly well alone, whereas the fungus seldom thrives without its partner. Their view is that the fungus is a controlled parasite that has learned to farm its captive. Whatever the verdict, lichens are astonishingly hardy. They colonise bare rock, survive desiccation for years, and absorb pollutants directly from the air because they lack roots and a protective cuticle. This last trait has made them valuable bioindicators; the disappearance of sensitive species from a city is a reliable, if unwelcome, sign of poor air quality.

passages.title: The Last Ferry
passages.text:
SCENE: A river jetty at dusk. A lone lamp flickers. MEERA stamps papers behind a wooden counter. DEVRAJ enters, soaked by the rain, clutching a battered suitcase.

DEVRAJ: One ticket across, please. The last ferry hasn't gone?

MEERA: (without looking up) It left an hour ago. Your watch, I suspect, has been telling you comfortable lies.

DEVRAJ: My watch stopped the day I left home. I have been walking by the sun, and the sun, it seems, is no better a timekeeper.

MEERA: The sun keeps perfect time. It is travellers who keep it waiting.

DEVRAJ: (setting down the suitcase) Then I shall wait for it again tomorrow. Is there a roof here that costs nothing?

MEERA: (pauses, stamps once more, then slides a key across the counter) Nothing, no. But the storeroom has a stove, and I have never yet charged a man for being cold.

DEVRAJ: You are kinder than your counter suggests.

MEERA: (dryly) The counter is paid for by the government. The kindness is unfunded.

passages.title: The Quiet Subsidy
passages.text: Every budget season, the municipal library is invited to justify itself in the currency its critics prefer: footfall, circulation, cost per visitor. By these measures it performs modestly, and some councillors have concluded that shelves of paper are a Victorian indulgence in an age of free search engines. This reasoning mistakes a tool for an institution. A search engine answers the question a person already knows how to ask; a library, through its stock, its staff and its silence, teaches the person which questions exist. The child who wanders into the wrong aisle and emerges with a book on beekeeping has been educated by serendipity, a commodity no algorithm tuned to past behaviour can reliably supply. Nor is the library merely a repository. For job-seekers without home internet, for pensioners escaping an empty flat, for students lacking a desk at home, it functions as a public room where nothing is demanded and no purchase is expected. Such value is real but diffuse, and diffuse benefits are precisely what narrow audits fail to record. To close a branch is to save a modest sum while quietly cancelling a service whose worth will be discovered only once it is gone.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a non-defining relative clause correctly?
options: My only brother who lives in Pune is a chemist.
My brother, that lives in Pune, is a chemist.
My only brother, who lives in Pune, is a chemist.
My only brother, which lives in Pune, is a chemist.
questions.explanation: A non-defining clause adds extra information, is set off by commas and uses who (not that) for a person. Option 1 is a defining pattern (it implies several brothers), option 2 wrongly uses "that" after a comma, and option 3 uses "which" for a person.

questions.question: Rewrite as a complex sentence: "Despite his being rich, he lives frugally."
options: Although he is rich, he lives frugally.
He is rich, yet he lives frugally.
He is rich but he lives frugally.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence has a subordinate clause: "Although he is rich" is a concession clause attached to the main clause. The other options are compound (yet/but) or a simple sentence with a participial phrase.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of: "Let us go for a trek," said Mohan.
options: Mohan ordered them to go for a trek.
Mohan said that let them go for a trek.
Mohan asked them if they go for a trek.
Mohan suggested that they should go for a trek.
questions.explanation: An imperative beginning with "Let us" expresses a proposal, reported with "suggested/proposed that + should". The other options change it into an order, keep the "let" form or make it a question.

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: "Not until the last guest had left ___."
options: she began to clean the hall
did she begin to clean the hall
she did begin to clean the hall
began she to clean the hall
questions.explanation: When "Not until" + clause opens a sentence, the main clause takes auxiliary inversion: "did she begin". The other options keep normal order or invert without the auxiliary.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: "Had the signal been repaired earlier, the passengers ___ stranded at this station even now."
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional: a past unreal condition (inverted "Had ... been repaired") with a present result ("even now"), so "would not be". "Would not have been" refers to a past result only; "will not be" and "had not been" do not fit the unreal pattern.

questions.question: Choose the correct reply: "Is the library open on Sundays?" "I'm afraid ___; the notice says it closes at weekends."
questions.explanation: After verbs like "afraid, hope, suppose, believe" the negative substitute for a whole clause is "not" (I'm afraid not). "So" would affirm; "it not" and "no" are ungrammatical here.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "He has ___ patience left; he is about to quit."
questions.explanation: "Little" (without "a") has a negative sense (almost none) and is used with uncountable nouns, matching "about to quit". "A little" means some; "few/a few" are used with countable nouns.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal: "The train was cancelled that day, so he ___ have taken it."
questions.explanation: "Can't have + V3" expresses a logical impossibility in the past, which suits the known fact that the train was cancelled. "Must have" expresses certainty that it happened; "might have" a possibility; "should have" criticism or expectation.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: "I ___ this novel for three weeks and still have fifty pages left."
questions.explanation: A continuing action from the past up to now with a duration ("for three weeks") takes the present perfect continuous. "Am reading" cannot be used with "for three weeks"; "had read" would imply completion.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling participle?
options: Walking down the road, a snake startled me.
Walking down the road, I was startled by a snake.
While I was walking down the road, a snake startled me.
Having finished the exam, the students were allowed to leave.
questions.explanation: In the first sentence the participial phrase "Walking down the road" seems to modify "a snake", which is illogical, so it dangles. In the others the phrase correctly attaches to "I" or "the students", or is a full clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: "This is one of the best novels that ___ been written on the Partition."
questions.explanation: In "one of the + plural noun + that/who", the relative pronoun refers to the plural noun (novels), so the verb is plural: "have been written". "Has" would refer to "one"; "was/is" do not fit the perfect passive.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: "By the time the rescue team arrived, the miners ___ trapped for nearly two days."
questions.explanation: Two past events are related and the trapping began before the arrival, so the past perfect "had been trapped" is needed. Simple past or present perfect do not show the earlier-in-the-past relationship.

questions.question: In "What troubled the examiners was that the answers were identical", the clause "that the answers were identical" is a:
options: noun clause used as subject complement
noun clause used as object of a verb
questions.explanation: The clause follows the linking verb "was" and completes the subject "What troubled the examiners", so it is a noun clause functioning as subject complement. It does not modify a noun, give a reason, or act as object.

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: "So absorbed ___ in the novel that she missed her stop."
questions.explanation: After a fronted "So + adjective" the verb "be" is inverted with its subject: "So absorbed was she in the novel...". "She was" keeps normal order, while "did/had she" use the wrong auxiliary.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "The teacher suggested that the student ___ the assignment again."
questions.explanation: After verbs of suggestion/recommendation the mandative subjunctive uses the base form (submit) for all persons, so "submits" is not used. Past or continuous forms do not fit this pattern.

questions.question: In academic writing, the lexical bundle "on the grounds that" is used to introduce:
questions.explanation: "On the grounds that" means "because / for the reason that", so it introduces a justification. Contrast uses "whereas", example uses "for instance", concession "even though".

questions.question: The idiom "to sail close to the wind" means:
options: to travel by a sailing ship
to take a risk by behaving almost improperly
questions.explanation: In sailing, steering very near the direction of the wind risks losing control; figuratively, it means doing something risky or close to the limits of what is acceptable.

questions.question: "He lit a nervous cigarette." The figure of speech used is:
questions.explanation: The adjective "nervous" really describes the man, but it is transferred to the cigarette (transferred epithet). No part stands for the whole (synecdoche), no understatement by negation (litotes) and no contradictory pair (oxymoron).

questions.question: The root "locut/loqu" in "circumlocution" means:
questions.explanation: "Locut/loqu" is Latin for "speak" (as in eloquent, loquacious). "Circumlocution" is speaking in a roundabout way.

questions.question: In which sentence is "sanction" used in the sense of "permit or approve"?
options: Several nations imposed sanctions on the regime.
The treaty provides for sanctions against violators.
The ministry has sanctioned a grant for the school.
The firm faced heavy sanctions for the breach.
questions.explanation: "Sanction" is a contronym: it can mean "approve" or "penalty". Only the third sentence uses the verb in the sense of approving. The others use the noun as a penalty.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation: "The government has ___ a crackdown on illegal mining."
questions.explanation: A crackdown is "launched" (or "mounted"); "thrown", "opened" and "shot" do not collocate with "crackdown".

questions.question: Which sentence uses a verb formed by conversion (zero derivation) from a noun?
options: He tried to widen the road.
questions.explanation: "Parachute" is a noun that became a verb with no change in form (conversion). "Enlighten", "modernise" and "widen" are formed by adding affixes to words.

questions.question: Which expression is used to hedge (soften) a claim in academic writing?
options: beyond a shadow of a doubt
questions.explanation: "To a certain extent" limits the strength of a claim. The other bundles intensify certainty or force.

questions.question: "To throw down the gauntlet" means:
questions.explanation: In medieval custom a knight threw down his glove (gauntlet) to challenge another to a duel, hence "to issue a challenge". Picking it up meant accepting the challenge.

questions.question: "We shape our tools, and afterwards our tools shape us." The figure of speech is:
questions.explanation: The words are repeated in reverse order (shape-tools / tools-shape), an A-B-B-A pattern known as chiasmus. Antithesis opposes ideas; anaphora repeats initial words; epistrophe repeats final words.

questions.question: "Podium" and "tripod" share a Greek root meaning:
questions.explanation: Both words come from Greek pous/pod- "foot" (a podium is a raised base to stand on; a tripod has three feet). Hand is manu/chir-, head is capit-/cephal-, sound is phon-.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "The police seized a cache of ___ drugs."
questions.explanation: "Illicit" means illegal or forbidden. "Elicit" is to draw out, "implicit" means implied, and "explicit" means clearly stated.

questions.question: Complete the collocation: "He chose to ___ a blind eye to the corruption."
questions.explanation: The fixed idiom is "turn a blind eye (to)", meaning deliberately ignore. The other verbs do not form the idiom.

questions.question: In "No one but Ravi knew the answer", the word "but" is used as a:
questions.explanation: Here "but" means "except" and takes the noun "Ravi" as its object, so it functions as a preposition. As a conjunction it would join clauses.

questions.question: A person described as "a dog in the manger" is one who:
options: serves his master faithfully but lazily
stops others from using something he cannot use himself
is timid in front of strangers
questions.explanation: From Aesop's fable of a dog that lay in the hay and would not let the ox eat it, though the dog itself could not eat hay: a spiteful person who blocks others from enjoying what he has no use for.

questions.question: Which of the following statements runs counter to the information given in the passage?
options: Lichens' lack of a cuticle makes them sensitive to air pollutants.
Botanists welcomed Schwendener's dual hypothesis as soon as it was proposed.
In the laboratory the alga can often survive without the fungus.
The fungus helps the lichen to hold on to rock and retain moisture.
questions.explanation: The passage says many botanists resisted the hypothesis for decades, so immediate welcome is contradicted. The other three statements are supported directly.

questions.question: The statement that the mutualism label "flatters the fungus" suggests that the label:
options: praises the fungus for being cleverer than the alga
compares the fungus's behaviour with human vanity
presents the fungus as a more benign partner than it really is
ranks the fungus above the alga in importance
questions.explanation: Critics think the fungus is really a controlled parasite, so calling it a mutualist makes it look kinder than it is. The passage does not discuss vanity, cleverness or ranking.

questions.question: The word "desiccation" in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Surviving "desiccation for years" on bare rock refers to extreme loss of water. Freezing, starvation and poisoning are not what the word means.

questions.question: The author's attitude to the debate over mutualism is best described as:
options: uncritical acceptance of the mutualism view
reporting a dispute without taking a side
questions.explanation: The phrase "Whatever the verdict" shows the author presents both views and moves on without committing. There is no sign of acceptance, hostility or amusement.

questions.question: The argument that the fungus is a "controlled parasite" rests chiefly on the observation that:
options: the fungus absorbs pollutants from the air
lichens lack roots and a protective cuticle
the alga can often live alone but the fungus seldom thrives without it
questions.explanation: The dependency is one-sided: the alga survives alone in culture while the fungus does not, which supports the parasite view. The other options are unrelated to this argument.

questions.question: Meera's remark that Devraj's watch has been "telling you comfortable lies" implies that:
options: the watch had shown an earlier time, giving him false reassurance
Devraj had deliberately lied about the time
questions.explanation: Devraj believed he was in time because of the stopped/incorrect watch; the "lies" were comforting because they falsely reassured him. The text gives no hint of deliberate lying, theft or general distrust.

questions.question: "The sun keeps perfect time. It is travellers who keep it waiting." In this reply Meera:
options: agrees that the sun is an unreliable guide
turns Devraj's complaint around to blame the traveller
questions.explanation: Devraj blamed the sun as a timekeeper; Meera inverts this, saying the fault lies with travellers who are late. She does not endorse his view.

questions.question: Meera's tone in the extract is best described as:
options: dryly witty, hiding a kind nature
questions.explanation: Her sharp, ironic remarks ("comfortable lies", "unfunded kindness") are accompanied by the generous act of giving the key, so the dry wit masks warmth.

questions.question: "The counter is paid for by the government. The kindness is unfunded." The last line suggests that:
options: Meera will charge Devraj for the storeroom later
the government has refused to fund the ferry
Meera is angry about her salary
her official duty and her personal generosity are separate things
questions.explanation: Her job (the counter) is official, but her help is personal and given at her own cost ("unfunded"). The other options are not supported.

questions.question: The stage direction "(pauses, stamps once more, then slides a key across the counter)" suggests that Meera:
options: hesitates briefly before choosing to help
is acting against her own wishes
questions.explanation: The pause followed by the key shows a short moment of deliberation, after which she decides to help. It does not show distraction or unwillingness.

questions.question: The main purpose of the editorial is to argue that:
options: libraries should charge visitors a fee
the value of a library cannot be captured by narrow performance measures
questions.explanation: The editorial opposes judging libraries only by footfall and cost, saying their benefits are real but diffuse. It does not call for replacing search engines or charging fees.

questions.question: "This reasoning mistakes a tool for an institution" means that the argument:
options: treats a device for finding information as equal to a social body with wider roles
wrongly assumes search engines are costly
questions.explanation: The author says a search engine is only a tool, whereas a library is an institution that also teaches, shelters and welcomes. The mistake is treating them as equivalent.

questions.question: The example of the child and the book on beekeeping is used to illustrate:
options: learning by serendipity that algorithms cannot reliably give
the popularity of hobbies among children
questions.explanation: The author calls it "education by serendipity", a benefit that algorithms tuned to past behaviour cannot supply. The other options are not the point of the example.

questions.question: The author would most likely disagree with which of the following?
options: A library offers value that audits fail to record.
Search engines make libraries entirely unnecessary.
Serendipity can be a genuine educational benefit.
Libraries serve people who lack home internet or a quiet desk.
questions.explanation: The editorial says a search engine only answers questions already known to the user and that libraries do more, so "entirely unnecessary" contradicts the author's view. The other three are views the author expresses.

questions.question: The word "diffuse" in "Such value is real but diffuse" most nearly means:
options: widely spread and hard to pinpoint
questions.explanation: The benefits are spread across many users and hard to measure, which is why audits miss them. "Concentrated" is the opposite, and the author says the value is real, not imaginary.

questions.question: In second language acquisition research, "intake" refers to:
questions.questionHi: द्वितीय भाषा-अर्जन के शोध में "intake" का अर्थ है:
options: the part of the input that the learner actually processes and takes in
all the language the learner hears or reads
the learner's spoken and written production
the grammar rules explained by the teacher
optionsHi: इनपुट का वह भाग जिसे शिक्षार्थी वास्तव में संसाधित कर आत्मसात करता है
वह सारी भाषा जो शिक्षार्थी सुनता या पढ़ता है
शिक्षार्थी का बोला या लिखा गया उत्पादन
questions.explanation: Input is everything the learner is exposed to; intake (Corder) is the portion that is noticed, processed and incorporated into the developing system. Output is production, and rules explained by the teacher are instruction.
questions.explanationHi: इनपुट वह सब है जिसके संपर्क में शिक्षार्थी आता है; intake (कॉर्डर) उसका वह अंश है जिस पर ध्यान जाता है, जो संसाधित होता और विकसित हो रही भाषा-प्रणाली में समा जाता है। उत्पादन output है और शिक्षक के समझाए नियम निर्देश हैं।

questions.question: In Cummins' framework, CALP differs from BICS in that CALP is:
questions.questionHi: कमिंस (Cummins) के ढाँचे में CALP, BICS से इस प्रकार भिन्न है कि CALP है:
options: everyday conversational fluency gained in about two years
language used only in the playground
the cognitively demanding, context-reduced language of academic learning that takes several years to develop
optionsHi: लगभग दो वर्षों में प्राप्त रोज़मर्रा की बोलचाल की प्रवाहशीलता
केवल खेल के मैदान में प्रयुक्त भाषा
शैक्षणिक अधिगम की संज्ञानात्मक रूप से कठिन, संदर्भ-रहित भाषा, जिसके विकास में कई वर्ष लगते हैं
questions.explanation: BICS = Basic Interpersonal Communicative Skills (context-rich, about 1-2 years); CALP = Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (abstract, context-reduced, about 5-7 years). That is why a fluent talker may still struggle in textbooks.
questions.explanationHi: BICS = Basic Interpersonal Communicative Skills (संदर्भ-युक्त, लगभग 1-2 वर्ष); CALP = Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (अमूर्त, संदर्भ-रहित, लगभग 5-7 वर्ष)। इसीलिए अच्छा बोलने वाला बच्चा भी पाठ्यपुस्तकों में कठिनाई महसूस कर सकता है।

questions.question: A child repeatedly asks, "Why does the moon change shape?" Which of Halliday's functions of language is mainly served?
questions.questionHi: एक बच्चा बार-बार पूछता है, "चाँद का आकार क्यों बदलता है?" हैलिडे (Halliday) का भाषा-प्रकार्य मुख्यतः कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: The heuristic function uses language to explore and learn about the environment ("tell me why"). Instrumental is "I want", regulatory is controlling others' behaviour, imaginative is play and make-believe.
questions.explanationHi: Heuristic प्रकार्य में भाषा से वातावरण को जानने-समझने का प्रयास होता है ("बताओ क्यों")। Instrumental का अर्थ "मुझे चाहिए", Regulatory दूसरों के व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करना और Imaginative खेल व कल्पना है।

questions.question: Hymes proposed "communicative competence" mainly because Chomsky's idea of linguistic competence ignored:
questions.questionHi: हाइम्स (Hymes) ने "communicative competence" की अवधारणा मुख्यतः इसलिए दी क्योंकि चॉम्स्की की भाषिक योग्यता ने किसकी उपेक्षा की थी?
options: the number of words a speaker knows
the knowledge of what is appropriate in a given social context
optionsHi: वक्ता द्वारा जाने गए शब्दों की संख्या
किसी सामाजिक संदर्भ में क्या उपयुक्त है, इसका ज्ञान
questions.explanation: Hymes argued that a speaker must know not only what is grammatical but also what is feasible, appropriate and actually done in a speech community. Chomsky's ideal-speaker model left out this sociocultural dimension.
questions.explanationHi: हाइम्स के अनुसार वक्ता को केवल व्याकरणिक शुद्धता ही नहीं, बल्कि यह भी जानना चाहिए कि भाषा-समुदाय में क्या उपयुक्त है। चॉम्स्की के आदर्श-वक्ता मॉडल में यह सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक पक्ष छूट गया था।

questions.question: A learner forgets the word "umbrella" and says "the thing we use against rain". Which component of Canale and Swain's model is at work?
questions.questionHi: एक शिक्षार्थी "umbrella" शब्द भूल जाता है और कहता है "वह चीज़ जो बारिश से बचने के लिए उपयोग करते हैं।" कैनेल और स्वेन (Canale & Swain) के मॉडल का कौन-सा घटक कार्य कर रहा है?
questions.explanation: Strategic competence is the ability to compensate for gaps by paraphrase, gestures or circumlocution. Grammatical concerns rules; sociolinguistic appropriateness; discourse the coherence of longer text.
questions.explanationHi: रणनीतिक सक्षमता का अर्थ है कमी को पैराफ्रेज़, इशारों या घुमाकर कहने से पूरा करना। व्याकरणिक सक्षमता नियमों से, सामाजिक-भाषिक उपयुक्तता से और प्रवचन सक्षमता लंबे पाठ की संगति से संबंधित है।

questions.question: Unlike contrastive analysis, error analysis:
questions.questionHi: Contrastive analysis के विपरीत, Error analysis:
options: studies learners' actual errors, many of which are not due to L1 interference
predicts errors only by comparing the L1 and L2 systems
treats every error as a sign of laziness
assumes all errors arise from mother-tongue transfer
optionsHi: शिक्षार्थियों की वास्तविक त्रुटियों का अध्ययन करता है, जिनमें से कई मातृभाषा-हस्तक्षेप के कारण नहीं होतीं
केवल L1 और L2 प्रणालियों की तुलना से त्रुटियों का पूर्वानुमान लगाता है
हर त्रुटि को आलस्य का संकेत मानता है
मानता है कि सभी त्रुटियाँ मातृभाषा-अंतरण से आती हैं
questions.explanation: Contrastive analysis predicts difficulty from L1-L2 differences, whereas error analysis (Corder) examines real learner output and finds intralingual errors (overgeneralisation) as well as interlingual ones.
questions.explanationHi: Contrastive analysis L1-L2 अंतर से कठिनाई का अनुमान लगाता है, जबकि Error analysis (कॉर्डर) वास्तविक लेखन/बोलचाल का विश्लेषण करता है और अंतःभाषिक त्रुटियों (जैसे अतिसामान्यीकरण) को भी पहचानता है।

questions.question: An advanced learner continues to say "He go to office" despite years of exposure and correction. This persistent non-target form is called:
questions.questionHi: एक उन्नत शिक्षार्थी वर्षों के अनुभव और सुधार के बावजूद "He go to office" कहता रहता है। इस स्थायी गलत प्रयोग को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.explanation: Selinker used "fossilisation" for incorrect interlanguage forms that become permanent and resist further instruction. A slip is occasional, overgeneralisation is a stage, code-switching is alternating languages.
questions.explanationHi: सेलिंकर ने "fossilisation" शब्द उन गलत अंतर्भाषा रूपों के लिए दिया जो स्थायी हो जाते हैं और शिक्षण से भी नहीं बदलते। चूक कभी-कभार होती है, अतिसामान्यीकरण एक चरण है, कोड-स्विचिंग दो भाषाओं का मिश्रण है।

questions.question: In the Anderson-Krathwohl revised taxonomy, a task in which students write an original short story using given vocabulary belongs to which level?
questions.questionHi: एंडरसन-क्रेथवॉल के संशोधित वर्गीकरण में, दिए गए शब्दों से मौलिक लघु कथा लिखना किस स्तर का कार्य है?
questions.explanation: In the revised taxonomy "Create" (producing something new) is the highest level, replacing "Synthesis". Evaluate means judging, analyse means breaking into parts, apply means using a procedure.
questions.explanationHi: संशोधित वर्गीकरण में "Create" (कुछ नया बनाना) सर्वोच्च स्तर है, जिसने "Synthesis" का स्थान लिया। Evaluate का अर्थ निर्णय देना, Analyse का भागों में तोड़ना और Apply का प्रक्रिया लागू करना है।

questions.question: Which is the best example of scaffolding in a reading lesson?
questions.questionHi: पठन-पाठ में scaffolding का सर्वोत्तम उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: Giving the answers directly to students
Making students read silently without any help
Giving prediction prompts and sentence starters, then gradually withdrawing support as learners gain confidence
optionsHi: छात्रों को सीधे उत्तर बता देना
बिना किसी सहायता के छात्रों से मौन पठन कराना
पूर्वानुमान संकेत व वाक्य-आरंभ देना और आत्मविश्वास बढ़ने पर सहायता धीरे-धीरे हटाना
questions.explanation: Scaffolding (Bruner, from Vygotsky's ZPD) is temporary, adjustable support that is gradually removed. Telling answers removes the thinking; no help ignores the ZPD; constant correction does not build independence.
questions.explanationHi: Scaffolding (ब्रूनर, वाइगोत्स्की के ZPD पर आधारित) अस्थायी और समायोज्य सहायता है जिसे धीरे-धीरे हटाया जाता है। उत्तर बताना सोचने से वंचित करता है, सहायता न देना ZPD की उपेक्षा है।

questions.question: CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning) is best described as:
questions.questionHi: CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning) का सर्वोत्तम वर्णन है:
options: a dual-focused approach teaching a subject through an additional language
teaching the mother tongue as a school subject
a method that bans all use of L1
optionsHi: अनुवाद के द्वारा व्याकरण नियम पढ़ाना
एक द्विलक्षी उपागम जिसमें विषय-वस्तु को अतिरिक्त भाषा के माध्यम से पढ़ाया जाता है
मातृभाषा को विषय के रूप में पढ़ाना
ऐसी विधि जो L1 का प्रयोग पूरी तरह रोकती है
questions.explanation: CLIL has two aims at once: learning subject content (e.g. science) and learning the additional language used to teach it. It is not translation-based and does not necessarily ban L1.
questions.explanationHi: CLIL के दो लक्ष्य एक साथ होते हैं: विषय-वस्तु (जैसे विज्ञान) सीखना और उसे पढ़ाने वाली अतिरिक्त भाषा सीखना। यह अनुवाद-आधारित नहीं है और L1 पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध नहीं लगाता।

questions.question: In a multilingual class, "translanguaging" refers to:
questions.questionHi: बहुभाषी कक्षा में "translanguaging" का अर्थ है:
options: the strategic use of learners' whole linguistic repertoire to support learning
punishing students who use their home language
translating every sentence word for word
optionsHi: सीखने में सहायता के लिए शिक्षार्थियों के संपूर्ण भाषिक भंडार का रणनीतिक उपयोग
घर की भाषा बोलने वाले छात्रों को दंड देना
हर वाक्य का शब्दशः अनुवाद करना
questions.explanation: Translanguaging treats a bilingual's languages as one integrated resource, which teachers use flexibly to build understanding. The other options describe bans or mechanical translation.
questions.explanationHi: Translanguaging द्विभाषी की भाषाओं को एक समेकित संसाधन मानती है, जिसे शिक्षक समझ बनाने के लिए लचीले ढंग से उपयोग करते हैं। अन्य विकल्प प्रतिबंध या यांत्रिक अनुवाद बताते हैं।

questions.question: The first step in a remedial programme for learners with weak spelling should be:
questions.questionHi: कमज़ोर वर्तनी वाले शिक्षार्थियों के लिए उपचारात्मक कार्यक्रम का पहला चरण होना चाहिए:
options: setting a common dictation for the class
analysing their errors to identify the specific areas of difficulty
optionsHi: बार-बार होने वाली गलतियों पर दंड देना
पूरी कक्षा के लिए एक सामान्य श्रुतलेख रखना
उनकी त्रुटियों का विश्लेषण कर कठिनाई के विशिष्ट क्षेत्र पहचानना
questions.explanation: Remedial teaching begins with diagnosis: find the pattern (silent letters, vowel digraphs etc.) and then plan targeted practice. More homework or punishment is not diagnostic.
questions.explanationHi: उपचारात्मक शिक्षण निदान से शुरू होता है: त्रुटि का प्रतिरूप (मौन अक्षर, स्वर-युग्म आदि) पहचानना और फिर लक्षित अभ्यास बनाना। अधिक गृहकार्य या दंड निदान नहीं है।

questions.question: Krashen's Monitor Hypothesis states that:
questions.questionHi: क्रैशन (Krashen) की Monitor Hypothesis कहती है कि:
options: learned knowledge acts only as an editor of output, used when time, focus on form and rule knowledge are available
acquisition and learning are the same process
optionsHi: सीखा हुआ ज्ञान धाराप्रवाह बोलचाल शुरू करता है
सीखा हुआ ज्ञान केवल अभिव्यक्ति का संपादक है, जो समय, रूप पर ध्यान और नियम-ज्ञान होने पर प्रयुक्त होता है
अर्जन और अधिगम एक ही प्रक्रिया हैं
चिंता अर्जन में सहायक होती है
questions.explanation: For Krashen, fluency comes from acquisition; conscious learning only monitors/edits what was produced. Learning does not turn into acquisition, and anxiety raises the affective filter.
questions.explanationHi: क्रैशन के अनुसार प्रवाह अर्जन से आता है; सचेत अधिगम केवल उत्पन्न भाषा की निगरानी/संपादन करता है। अधिगम अर्जन में नहीं बदलता और चिंता affective filter को बढ़ाती है।

questions.question: Lenneberg's Critical Period Hypothesis suggests that:
questions.questionHi: लेनेबर्ग की Critical Period Hypothesis के अनुसार:
options: language can be acquired equally easily at any age
only adults can acquire a second language
language acquisition depends only on classroom teaching
natural language acquisition is easiest before puberty, after which biological readiness declines
optionsHi: भाषा किसी भी आयु में समान रूप से आसानी से अर्जित की जा सकती है
केवल वयस्क ही द्वितीय भाषा अर्जित कर सकते हैं
भाषा-अर्जन केवल कक्षा-शिक्षण पर निर्भर है
यौवनारंभ से पहले स्वाभाविक भाषा-अर्जन सबसे आसान होता है, उसके बाद जैविक तत्परता घटती है
questions.explanation: The hypothesis links language acquisition to a biologically limited window ending around puberty; later learning generally needs more effort and rarely reaches native-like levels. It is a hypothesis with debated evidence for L2 learning.
questions.explanationHi: यह परिकल्पना भाषा-अर्जन को यौवनारंभ के आसपास समाप्त होने वाली जैविक समय-सीमा से जोड़ती है; बाद में सीखने में अधिक प्रयास लगता है और मातृभाषा-जैसा स्तर कम ही मिलता है। द्वितीय भाषा के लिए इसके प्रमाणों पर बहस है।

questions.question: Long's Interaction Hypothesis stresses that acquisition is helped by:
questions.questionHi: लॉन्ग (Long) की Interaction Hypothesis के अनुसार अर्जन में सहायक है:
options: negotiation of meaning through clarification requests and comprehension checks
optionsHi: स्पष्टीकरण के अनुरोध और बोध-जाँच द्वारा अर्थ की वार्ता (negotiation of meaning)
questions.explanation: Long held that conversational interaction in which partners negotiate meaning makes input comprehensible and draws attention to form. Silent reading, memorising and drilling lack such negotiation.
questions.explanationHi: लॉन्ग का मत था कि जब वार्ताकार अर्थ की वार्ता करते हैं तो इनपुट बोधगम्य बनता है और रूप पर ध्यान जाता है। मौन पठन, रटना और ड्रिल में ऐसी वार्ता नहीं होती।

questions.question: A 15-year-old girl tries out different roles and peer groups while struggling to decide who she is. According to Erikson, which crisis is she facing?
questions.questionHi: एक 15 वर्षीय लड़की स्वयं को समझने के लिए अलग-अलग भूमिकाएँ और मित्र-समूह आज़माती है। एरिक्सन के अनुसार वह किस संकट का सामना कर रही है?
questions.explanation: Adolescence (about 12-18 years) is the stage of identity vs role confusion. Industry vs inferiority belongs to 6-12 years, intimacy vs isolation to young adulthood, initiative vs guilt to 3-6 years.
questions.explanationHi: किशोरावस्था (लगभग 12-18 वर्ष) पहचान बनाम भूमिका-भ्रम की अवस्था है। उद्यमिता बनाम हीनता 6-12 वर्ष, घनिष्ठता बनाम अलगाव युवावस्था और पहल बनाम अपराध-बोध 3-6 वर्ष की अवस्था है।

questions.question: According to Vygotsky, private speech (self-talk) in young children serves mainly to:
questions.questionHi: वाइगोत्स्की के अनुसार छोटे बच्चों की निजी वाणी (self-talk) मुख्यतः किसलिए होती है?
options: show a delay in language development
guide and regulate the child's own thinking and action
optionsHi: कक्षा में अन्य बच्चों को परेशान करना
बिना अर्थ के बड़ों की नकल करना
बच्चे की अपनी सोच और क्रिया को निर्देशित व नियंत्रित करना
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw private speech as a tool of thought that later becomes silent inner speech, helping children plan and self-regulate. Piaget, by contrast, called it egocentric speech. It is not a sign of delay or mere imitation.
questions.explanationHi: वाइगोत्स्की ने निजी वाणी को चिंतन का साधन माना जो आगे चलकर मौन आंतरिक वाणी बन जाती है और बच्चे को योजना बनाने व स्व-नियमन में मदद करती है। पियाजे इसे अहंकेंद्रित वाणी कहते थे। यह देरी या केवल नकल का संकेत नहीं है।

questions.question: Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence consists of which three components?
questions.questionHi: स्टर्नबर्ग के त्रिसूत्री बुद्धि सिद्धांत (triarchic theory) के तीन घटक कौन-से हैं?
questions.explanation: Sternberg's three aspects are analytical (componential), creative (experiential) and practical (contextual) intelligence. The other sets belong to different models (Thurstone-type, Cattell, Gardner).
questions.explanationHi: स्टर्नबर्ग के तीन पक्ष हैं: विश्लेषणात्मक, सृजनात्मक और व्यावहारिक बुद्धि। अन्य समुच्चय दूसरे मॉडलों (थर्स्टन-प्रकार, कैटेल, गार्डनर) के हैं।

questions.question: Which ability, according to Cattell, tends to decline after early adulthood, while accumulated knowledge continues to grow?
questions.questionHi: कैटेल के अनुसार कौन-सी योग्यता प्रारंभिक वयस्कता के बाद घटने लगती है, जबकि संचित ज्ञान बढ़ता रहता है?
questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence (novel reasoning, speed) peaks early and declines, while crystallised intelligence (knowledge and vocabulary from experience) continues to grow. Emotional and practical intelligence are not Cattell's terms.
questions.explanationHi: तरल बुद्धि (नई समस्याओं में तर्क, गति) जल्दी चरम पर पहुँचकर घटती है, जबकि मूर्त बुद्धि (अनुभव से प्राप्त ज्ञान व शब्दावली) बढ़ती रहती है। भावनात्मक और व्यावहारिक बुद्धि कैटेल की शब्दावली नहीं हैं।

questions.question: Which test best measures Guilford's "divergent production"?
questions.questionHi: गिलफोर्ड के "अपसारी उत्पादन" (divergent production) को कौन-सा परीक्षण सबसे अच्छे ढंग से मापता है?
options: A task asking students to list as many uses of a brick as possible
optionsHi: एक ईंट के अधिकाधिक उपयोग सूचीबद्ध करने का कार्य
questions.explanation: Divergent production means generating many varied answers to an open problem (fluency, flexibility, originality), as in the "alternate uses" task. The other tests have a single correct answer or measure memory or speed.
questions.explanationHi: अपसारी उत्पादन का अर्थ खुली समस्या के अनेक विविध उत्तर देना (प्रवाह, लचीलापन, मौलिकता) है, जैसे "वैकल्पिक उपयोग" कार्य। अन्य परीक्षणों में एक सही उत्तर होता है या स्मृति/गति मापी जाती है।

questions.question: A 6-month-old baby repeatedly shakes a rattle to hear the sound. In Piaget's scheme this is:
questions.questionHi: 6 माह का शिशु आवाज़ सुनने के लिए झुनझुने को बार-बार हिलाता है। पियाजे की योजना में यह है:
questions.explanation: Secondary circular reactions (about 4-8 months) repeat actions to produce interesting effects on objects outside the body. Primary ones centre on the infant's own body, tertiary ones (12-18 months) involve deliberate variation and experimentation.
questions.explanationHi: द्वितीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ (लगभग 4-8 माह) शरीर के बाहर की वस्तुओं पर रोचक प्रभाव पैदा करने के लिए क्रियाओं की पुनरावृत्ति हैं। प्राथमिक का केंद्र शिशु का अपना शरीर और तृतीयक (12-18 माह) में जानबूझकर बदलाव व प्रयोग होते हैं।

questions.question: A teacher gives the same test to the same group after two weeks and correlates the two sets of scores. This estimates:
questions.questionHi: एक शिक्षक वही परीक्षण उसी समूह को दो सप्ताह बाद देता है और दोनों अंक-समूहों का सहसंबंध निकालता है। इससे क्या आकलित होता है?
questions.explanation: Repeating the same test after an interval and correlating scores gives test-retest reliability (stability). Split-half divides one administration; inter-rater compares scorers; content validity is about coverage.
questions.explanationHi: वही परीक्षण अंतराल के बाद दोहराकर अंकों का सहसंबंध निकालने से परीक्षण-पुनर्परीक्षण विश्वसनीयता (स्थिरता) मिलती है। अर्ध-विभाजन एक ही प्रशासन को बाँटता है; अंतर-मूल्यांकनकर्ता में मूल्यांकनकर्ताओं की तुलना होती है।

questions.question: In item analysis, a discrimination index close to zero means that the item:
questions.questionHi: प्रश्न-विश्लेषण (item analysis) में विभेदन-सूचकांक शून्य के निकट होने का अर्थ है कि प्रश्न:
options: does not distinguish between high and low scorers
optionsHi: सभी के लिए बहुत सरल है
उच्च और निम्न अंक पाने वालों में अंतर नहीं करता
questions.explanation: Discrimination index shows how well an item separates high scorers from low scorers; near zero means both groups do equally well or badly. Ease or difficulty is shown by the difficulty index, not the discrimination index.
questions.explanationHi: विभेदन-सूचकांक बताता है कि प्रश्न उच्च और निम्न अंक वालों को कितना अलग करता है; शून्य के निकट का अर्थ है दोनों समूहों का प्रदर्शन समान। सरलता/कठिनता कठिनाई-सूचकांक से पता चलती है।

questions.question: A table of specifications (blueprint) in test construction mainly ensures:
questions.questionHi: परीक्षण-निर्माण में विनिर्देश-तालिका (blueprint) मुख्यतः क्या सुनिश्चित करती है?
questions.explanation: A blueprint distributes items across content areas and objectives, so the test samples the syllabus properly: content validity. Predictive and concurrent validity need an external criterion.
questions.explanationHi: Blueprint विषय-क्षेत्रों और उद्देश्यों में प्रश्नों का वितरण करता है ताकि परीक्षण पाठ्यक्रम का उचित प्रतिनिधित्व करे: यही विषय-वस्तु वैधता है। भविष्यसूचक व समवर्ती वैधता के लिए बाहरी कसौटी चाहिए।

questions.question: The "Holistic Progress Card" proposed in NEP 2020 is meant to report:
questions.questionHi: NEP 2020 में प्रस्तावित "समग्र प्रगति कार्ड" (Holistic Progress Card) किसका प्रतिवेदन देने के लिए है?
options: a 360-degree view of cognitive, affective and psychomotor progress, including self and peer assessment
optionsHi: आत्म और सहपाठी आकलन सहित संज्ञानात्मक, भावात्मक व मनोगत्यात्मक प्रगति का 360-डिग्री चित्र
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 envisages a multidimensional report with self-assessment, peer assessment and teacher assessment across domains, moving away from marks-only reporting.
questions.explanationHi: NEP 2020 में आत्म, सहपाठी और शिक्षक आकलन के साथ सभी क्षेत्रों की बहुआयामी रिपोर्ट की परिकल्पना है, जो केवल अंकों वाली रिपोर्टिंग से हटकर है।

questions.question: In the 5E instructional model, which phase comes immediately after "Engage"?
questions.questionHi: 5E शिक्षण-प्रतिमान में "Engage" के तुरंत बाद कौन-सा चरण आता है?
questions.explanation: The sequence is Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate. After arousing curiosity, learners explore materials or problems before explanations are formalised.
questions.explanationHi: क्रम है: Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate। जिज्ञासा जगाने के बाद शिक्षार्थी व्याख्या से पहले सामग्री या समस्याओं का अन्वेषण करते हैं।

questions.question: NCF-SE 2023 organises school education into which four stages, in order?
questions.questionHi: NCF-SE 2023 स्कूली शिक्षा को किन चार चरणों में, क्रमानुसार, व्यवस्थित करती है?
questions.explanation: NCF-SE 2023 follows the 5+3+3+4 design of NEP 2020: Foundational (ages 3-8), Preparatory (8-11), Middle (11-14) and Secondary (14-18).
questions.explanationHi: NCF-SE 2023 NEP 2020 की 5+3+3+4 संरचना का पालन करती है: आधारभूत (3-8 वर्ष), तैयारी (8-11), मध्य (11-14) और माध्यमिक (14-18)।

questions.question: In line with NCF 2005's move away from rote learning, the textbook should be treated as:
questions.questionHi: NCF 2005 के रटंत-शिक्षा से दूर जाने के अनुरूप, पाठ्यपुस्तक को किस रूप में देखा जाना चाहिए?
options: a list of questions for examination
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 recommends that the textbook be one of several resources (along with local material, libraries, activities) and not the sole source or the basis of examinations.
questions.explanationHi: NCF 2005 कहती है कि पाठ्यपुस्तक कई संसाधनों (स्थानीय सामग्री, पुस्तकालय, गतिविधियाँ) में से एक हो, न कि एकमात्र स्रोत या परीक्षा का आधार।

questions.question: Which classroom practice best reflects a constructivist view of learning?
questions.questionHi: रचनावादी अधिगम-दृष्टि को कक्षा का कौन-सा अभ्यास सबसे अच्छी तरह दर्शाता है?
options: Teacher solving every problem on the board
Students investigating a problem in groups with the teacher as facilitator
optionsHi: याद करने के लिए नोट्स लिखवाना
शिक्षक द्वारा बोर्ड पर हर समस्या हल करना
छात्रों द्वारा समूह में समस्या की जाँच, शिक्षक सुगमकर्ता के रूप में
questions.explanation: Constructivism holds that learners build knowledge actively through experience and social interaction, with the teacher guiding. The other options are transmission-based.
questions.explanationHi: रचनावाद के अनुसार शिक्षार्थी अनुभव और सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया से सक्रिय रूप से ज्ञान गढ़ते हैं और शिक्षक मार्गदर्शन देता है। अन्य विकल्प सूचना-हस्तांतरण पर आधारित हैं।

questions.question: Which approach best helps address gender stereotypes in the classroom?
questions.questionHi: कक्षा में लैंगिक रूढ़ियों को दूर करने के लिए कौन-सा तरीका सबसे उपयुक्त है?
options: Assigning cleaning duties only to girls
Using gender-neutral language and examples and ensuring equal participation
optionsHi: सफ़ाई का कार्य केवल लड़कियों को सौंपना
लिंग-निरपेक्ष भाषा व उदाहरणों का प्रयोग और समान भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करना
questions.explanation: Gender-sensitive teaching challenges stereotypes through inclusive language, varied role models and equal opportunities. Segregation and role-assignment reinforce stereotypes; avoidance leaves them unchallenged.
questions.explanationHi: लिंग-संवेदनशील शिक्षण समावेशी भाषा, विविध आदर्शों और समान अवसरों से रूढ़ियों को चुनौती देता है। अलगाव और भूमिकाओं का बँटवारा रूढ़ियों को मजबूत करते हैं; बचना उन्हें अनछुआ छोड़ देता है।

questions.question: 'महोत्सव' का सही संधि-विच्छेद है:
questions.explanation: महा + उत्सव में 'आ' और 'उ' मिलकर 'ओ' बनते हैं (गुण संधि), इसलिए महोत्सव। अन्य विच्छेद गलत हैं।

questions.question: 'चक्रपाणि' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: चक्र है पाणि (हाथ) में जिसके अर्थात् विष्णु: कोई तीसरा अर्थ प्रधान है, इसलिए बहुव्रीहि समास। अन्य समासों में पूर्व या उत्तर पद प्रधान होता है।

questions.question: लोकोक्ति 'कोयले की दलाली में हाथ काले' का अर्थ है:
options: कोयले का व्यापार लाभदायक होता है
हाथ गंदे होने पर काम बिगड़ना
बुरे काम या संगति से बदनामी मिलती ही है
questions.explanation: इसका आशय है कि बुरे काम या बुरे लोगों के साथ रहने पर कलंक अवश्य लगता है। अन्य विकल्प शाब्दिक अर्थ पर आधारित हैं।

questions.question: 'प्रणय' और 'परिणय' शब्दों के सही अर्थ क्रमशः हैं:
questions.explanation: प्रणय का अर्थ है प्रेम और परिणय का अर्थ है विवाह। अन्य विकल्पों में क्रम या अर्थ गलत है।

questions.question: नीरोग का सही संधि-विच्छेद है:
questions.explanation: निः + रोग में विसर्ग (र् से बना) के बाद र आने पर पहला र् लुप्त हो जाता है और पूर्व स्वर इ दीर्घ ई हो जाता है, इसलिए नीरोग। अन्य विच्छेद गलत हैं।

questions.question: One word for "a person who remains unaffected by pleasure and pain":
questions.explanation: A stoic bears pleasure and pain with calm. An epicure loves fine food, a hedonist pursues pleasure, and a cynic distrusts human motives.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: "She is senior ___ me by two years."
questions.explanation: Adjectives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take "to", not "than". So "senior to me".

questions.question: "To beard the lion in his den" means:
options: to confront a powerful person on his own ground
questions.explanation: The idiom means boldly confronting a powerful or fearsome person in his own territory. The other meanings are unrelated.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "obdurate":
questions.explanation: "Obdurate" means hard-hearted and stubborn. Its opposite is "compliant" (yielding). Adamant and stubborn are synonyms, and callous is close in sense.

questions.question: Fill in the articles: "She is ___ European and wishes to become ___ MLA."
questions.explanation: "European" begins with the sound /j/, so "a"; "MLA" begins with the vowel sound "em", so "an".

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 8, 5, 16, 7, 32, 9, ?
questions.explanation: Two interleaved series: odd places 3, 5, 7, 9 (add 2) and even places 8, 16, 32, ? (double). The next term is 32 x 2 = 64.

questions.question: A is B's brother. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is E related to A?
questions.questionHi: A, B का भाई है। C, B की माँ है। D, C के पिता हैं। E, D की माँ है। E का A से क्या संबंध है?
questions.explanation: A and B share mother C. D is C's father, so A's maternal grandfather. E is D's mother, so A's maternal great-grandmother.
questions.explanationHi: A और B की माँ C है। D, C के पिता हैं यानी A के नाना। E, D की माँ हैं यानी A की परनानी।

questions.question: Ravi walks 9 m west, turns right and walks 12 m, then turns right and walks 4 m. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.questionHi: रवि 9 मी. पश्चिम चलता है, दाएँ मुड़कर 12 मी. चलता है, फिर दाएँ मुड़कर 4 मी. चलता है। वह प्रारंभिक बिंदु से कितनी दूर है?
questions.explanation: West 9, then north 12, then east 4: net 5 m west and 12 m north. Distance = square root of (25 + 144) = 13 m.
questions.explanationHi: पश्चिम 9, फिर उत्तर 12, फिर पूर्व 4: शुद्ध 5 मी. पश्चिम और 12 मी. उत्तर। दूरी = वर्गमूल (25 + 144) = 13 मी.।

questions.question: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:40?
questions.questionHi: घड़ी में 3:40 बजे घंटे और मिनट की सुइयों के बीच कितना कोण होगा?
questions.explanation: Hour hand: 3 x 30 + 40 x 0.5 = 110 degrees. Minute hand: 40 x 6 = 240 degrees. Difference = 130 degrees.

questions.question: Statements: Some pens are books. No book is a table. Conclusions: I. Some pens are not tables. II. No pen is a table.
questions.questionHi: कथन: कुछ पेन किताबें हैं। कोई किताब मेज़ नहीं है। निष्कर्ष: I. कुछ पेन मेज़ नहीं हैं। II. कोई पेन मेज़ नहीं है।
optionsHi: केवल निष्कर्ष II अनुसरण करता है
केवल निष्कर्ष I अनुसरण करता है
I और II दोनों अनुसरण करते हैं
न I और न II अनुसरण करता है
questions.explanation: The pens that are books cannot be tables, so some pens are not tables (I follows). Other pens may or may not be tables, so "no pen is a table" (II) does not follow.
questions.explanationHi: जो पेन किताबें हैं वे मेज़ नहीं हो सकते, इसलिए कुछ पेन मेज़ नहीं हैं (I अनुसरण करता है)। अन्य पेन मेज़ हो भी सकते हैं, इसलिए "कोई पेन मेज़ नहीं" (II) अनुसरण नहीं करता।

questions.question: In MS Excel, =COUNTIF(A1:A10,">50") returns:
questions.questionHi: MS Excel में =COUNTIF(A1:A10,">50") क्या लौटाता है?
options: the number of cells in A1:A10 whose value is greater than 50
the sum of values greater than 50
optionsHi: A1:A10 में उन कोशिकाओं की संख्या जिनका मान 50 से अधिक है
questions.explanation: COUNTIF counts the cells meeting a criterion. Summing is SUMIF, averaging is AVERAGE/AVERAGEIF and the largest value is MAX.
questions.explanationHi: COUNTIF शर्त पूरी करने वाली कोशिकाएँ गिनता है। योग SUMIF, औसत AVERAGE/AVERAGEIF और सबसे बड़ा मान MAX देता है।

questions.question: The decimal equivalent of the binary number 1101101 is:
questions.questionHi: द्विआधारी संख्या 1101101 का दशमलव मान है:

questions.question: Which of the following is the fastest storage in a computer's memory hierarchy?
questions.questionHi: कंप्यूटर की मेमोरी-पदानुक्रम में सबसे तेज़ संग्रहण कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest (and smallest) storage, followed by cache, RAM and then secondary storage like SSD.
questions.explanationHi: रजिस्टर CPU के भीतर होते हैं और सबसे तेज़ (व सबसे छोटे) संग्रहण हैं; उसके बाद कैश, RAM और फिर SSD जैसा द्वितीयक संग्रहण आता है।

questions.question: Which shortcut inserts the current date into a cell in MS Excel?
questions.questionHi: MS Excel में सेल में वर्तमान तिथि डालने का शॉर्टकट कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + ; enters today's date. Ctrl + Shift + ; enters the current time, Ctrl + D fills down and Ctrl + T creates a table.
questions.explanationHi: Ctrl + ; आज की तिथि डालता है। Ctrl + Shift + ; वर्तमान समय डालता है, Ctrl + D नीचे की ओर भरता है और Ctrl + T तालिका बनाता है।

questions.question: A harmful program that appears useful, gets installed by the user and then secretly performs malicious actions without replicating itself is a:
questions.questionHi: ऐसा हानिकारक प्रोग्राम जो उपयोगी दिखता है, उपयोगकर्ता द्वारा इंस्टॉल हो जाता है और फिर चुपके से हानिकारक कार्य करता है, पर स्वयं की प्रतिलिपि नहीं बनाता, कहलाता है:
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software and does not self-replicate. Worms replicate across networks; boot-sector and macro viruses attach themselves to boot code or documents.
questions.explanationHi: ट्रोजन हॉर्स वैध सॉफ़्टवेयर का रूप धारण करता है और स्वयं की प्रतिलिपि नहीं बनाता। वर्म नेटवर्क में फैलते हैं; बूट-सेक्टर व मैक्रो वायरस बूट कोड या दस्तावेज़ों से जुड़ते हैं।

questions.question: The anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) was added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.questionHi: दल-बदल विरोधी कानून (दसवीं अनुसूची) संविधान में किस संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment (1985) inserted the Tenth Schedule on disqualification on grounds of defection. The 42nd was the "mini-Constitution", the 44th restored many freedoms and the 61st lowered the voting age to 18.
questions.explanationHi: 52वें संशोधन (1985) ने दल-बदल के आधार पर निरर्हता संबंधी दसवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी। 42वाँ "लघु संविधान" था, 44वें ने अनेक स्वतंत्रताएँ बहाल कीं और 61वें ने मतदान आयु 18 वर्ष की।

questions.question: Which is the highest peak of Peninsular India (south of the Vindhyas)?
questions.questionHi: प्रायद्वीपीय भारत (विंध्य के दक्षिण) की सबसे ऊँची चोटी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: Anamudi (about 2,695 m) in the Anamalai hills of Kerala is the highest peak of Peninsular India. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris, Mahendragiri is in the Eastern Ghats and Dhupgarh is in the Satpura range.
questions.explanationHi: केरल की अनाईमलाई पहाड़ियों में स्थित अनाईमुडी (लगभग 2,695 मी.) प्रायद्वीपीय भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी है। दोदाबेट्टा नीलगिरि की सबसे ऊँची, महेंद्रगिरि पूर्वी घाट में और धूपगढ़ सतपुड़ा श्रृंखला में है।

questions.question: The Mahanadi, the chief river of Chhattisgarh, rises near Sihawa in which district?
questions.questionHi: छत्तीसगढ़ की प्रमुख नदी महानदी का उद्गम सिहावा के निकट किस जिले में है?
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi rises from the Sihawa hills in Dhamtari district. Bastar's chief river is the Indravati; Kanker and Raigarh are not its source district.
questions.explanationHi: महानदी का उद्गम धमतरी जिले की सिहावा पहाड़ियों से होता है। बस्तर की प्रमुख नदी इंद्रावती है; कांकेर और रायगढ़ इसके उद्गम जिले नहीं हैं।

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-tax revenue receipt of the Union Government?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में कौन-सी केंद्र सरकार की गैर-कर राजस्व प्राप्ति है?
questions.explanation: Interest and dividends from loans and public enterprises are non-tax revenue. Corporation tax, customs duty and GST are tax revenue.
questions.explanationHi: ऋणों और सार्वजनिक उपक्रमों से प्राप्त ब्याज व लाभांश गैर-कर राजस्व है। निगम कर, सीमा शुल्क और GST कर-राजस्व हैं।

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is:
questions.questionHi: चुंबकीय अभिवाह घनत्व (magnetic flux density) का SI मात्रक है:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla (weber per square metre). Weber is the unit of flux, henry of inductance, and gauss is a CGS unit.
questions.explanationHi: चुंबकीय अभिवाह घनत्व टेस्ला (वेबर प्रति वर्ग मीटर) में मापा जाता है। वेबर अभिवाह, हेनरी प्रेरकत्व का मात्रक है और गॉस CGS मात्रक है।
